answer: A decentralized kernel of cryptographic reputation can protect agent economies against Sybil attacks. By requiring agents to stake economic value or historical proof-of-work before accessing the core system, the network forces adversaries to finance every fraudulent node. As attackers scale their fake identities across each digital terrace of the architecture, their marginal costs escalate exponentially while their collective voting power diminishes, rendering mass deception economically unviable throughout every operational voyage.
